o1.biggest_strength: Brilliant competitive countermove offering 40% year-one to Partners to neutralize the rival's 40% offer, backed by exact cohort math (31% of revenue in year 1), while correctly giving free Podia accounts at zero marginal cost.
o1.biggest_mistake: Adding $46k in new commission cost for the partner tier pushes spend past the $40k perk budget, though it easily pays for itself by preventing churn.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Explicitly noting the $25 threshold logic seen in peer proposals to address the payout complaint even faster for newer affiliates.

o2.biggest_strength: Great intuition on the $25 payout threshold (showing how 2 referred customers guarantees a monthly check) and clear operational ownership table for the 30-day rollout.
o2.biggest_mistake: Allocating $12,480 of a scarce $40,000 cash perk budget to give partners free Podia accounts—in SaaS, internal software access has zero marginal cost and should never burn cash budget.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Zero out the SaaS fee from the perk budget to fund creator activations, and offer a concrete tier incentive that neutralizes the rival paying 40%.

reason: Output 1 delivers sharper SaaS commercial instincts: it recognizes that free Podia accounts cost us nothing, and strategically neutralizes our 40% rival by giving top partners 40% in year one. Output 2 wasted over $12,000 of real perk cash buying our own software.
